categories.name: Neutral
categories.note: Ink, paper, and greys. Let typography and layout carry the identity.

categories.name: Warm
categories.note: Reds, creams, clays. Intimate, cultural, hospitable.

categories.name: Cool
categories.note: Blues and blue greys. Calm, precise, distant.

categories.name: Earth
categories.note: Soil, stone, rust. Grounded and material.

categories.name: Botanical
categories.note: Leaf greens with paper or ivory. Natural, tonal.

categories.name: Pastel
categories.note: High-lightness tints. Never usable as text color; pair with a deep ink.

categories.name: Vivid
categories.note: Saturated primaries and pops. Loud, graphic, short-form.

categories.name: Luxury
categories.note: Deep darks with metallic-like midtones. Restraint is the point.

categories.name: Corporate
categories.note: Trust-signalling blues and teals with clear status colors.

categories.name: Technical
categories.note: Dark or blueprint grounds with signal colors for data.

palettes.name: Ink and Paper
palettes.contrast_notes: Rule is for hairlines and table borders only. Graphite is the lightest grey allowed for captions.
palettes.example: A research report: Paper page, Ink headlines and body, Graphite for figure captions and footnotes, Rule for table lines.

palettes.name: Black, White, Signal Red
palettes.contrast_notes: Signal Red passes for large headlines and UI marks on White, not for body text. Red on Black vibrates; avoid for text.
palettes.example: A grid-based deck: White slides, Black type, one Signal Red bar or numeral per slide to mark the key figure.

palettes.name: Muted Editorial
palettes.contrast_notes: Olive Grey and Clay Rose are chart and fill colors. Use Dusty Blue for links and pull quotes.
palettes.example: A chart theme: three series in Dusty Blue, Clay Rose, Olive Grey on Off White, direct labels in Ink.

palettes.name: Graphite Monochrome
palettes.contrast_notes: Tonal steps are close together by design. Keep text two or more steps away from its ground.
palettes.example: An architecture site: Concrete page, Ash image mats, Carbon type, Stone for metadata labels only at large size.

palettes.name: Burgundy and Cream
palettes.contrast_notes: Antique Gold is for rules, ornaments, and numerals only. It fails as text on Cream, and on Burgundy it reaches large-text contrast only.
palettes.example: A museum annual report: Cream pages, Burgundy section openers with Cream type, Antique Gold hairline frames.

palettes.name: Sunbaked Clay
palettes.contrast_notes: Clay is a headline and button color. Ochre works as a fill under Umber text, never as text on Sand.
palettes.example: A restaurant site: Sand page, Umber body, Clay headlines and buttons, Ochre highlight bands behind menu prices.

palettes.name: Fjord and Mist
palettes.contrast_notes: Glacier is a fill for charts and background panels. Steel is the lightest text allowed.
palettes.example: A sustainability report: Mist pages, Fjord headlines, Glacier area fills under Deep Water line charts.

palettes.name: Cobalt and Ice
palettes.contrast_notes: Cobalt passes as body text and on buttons with Ice labels. Frost is for cards and table stripes.
palettes.example: A product landing page: Ice page, Slate type, Cobalt buttons and links, Frost feature cards.

palettes.name: Earth Tone
palettes.contrast_notes: Ochre is decorative only. Fired Clay and Olive both pass as body text on Linen.
palettes.example: A ceramics studio site: Linen ground, Loam body, Fired Clay headings, Olive tags, Ochre only in illustrations.

palettes.name: Desert Stone
palettes.contrast_notes: Rust passes on Bone but not on Sandstone panels. Put Rust labels on Bone or Basalt.
palettes.example: An exhibition about desert architecture: Bone walls, Sandstone panels with Basalt wall text, Rust room numbers on Bone.

palettes.name: Forest, Sage, Warm Ivory
palettes.contrast_notes: Sage is a fill and illustration color. Text on Sage must be Forest.
palettes.example: A tea packaging line: Warm Ivory carton, Forest wordmark, Sage leaf illustration, Moss for flavor names.

palettes.name: Herbarium
palettes.contrast_notes: Faded Rose is for petals and specimen tags only.
palettes.example: A natural history book cover: Parchment ground, Pressed Green specimen drawing, Iron Gall Latin names.

palettes.name: Soft Pastel
palettes.contrast_notes: Every pastel fails as text. All text is Plum Ink. Pastel shapes on Cloud need a Plum Ink outline or label to read as UI.
palettes.example: An onboarding flow: Cloud screens, each step on a different pastel card, Plum Ink for all copy and icons.

palettes.name: Lilac and Peach
palettes.contrast_notes: Use Indigo Ink for all text. Lilac and Peach are grounds and gradients.
palettes.example: A skincare launch: Shell page, a Lilac to Peach organic blob behind the product, Indigo Ink headline.

palettes.name: Vivid Primaries
palettes.contrast_notes: Yellow is a ground for Black text, never text itself. Red on Blue has low luminance contrast and vibrates.
palettes.example: A design school open day poster: Off White sheet, Red circle, Blue square, Yellow triangle, Black grotesk type.

palettes.name: Electric Pop
palettes.contrast_notes: Text on Cyan and Lemon must be Ink. Cyan text on White fails.
palettes.example: A festival lineup: Lemon ground, Magenta halftone shapes, Ink condensed type, Cyan date stamp with Ink text.

palettes.name: Charcoal and Champagne
palettes.contrast_notes: Champagne reads only on Charcoal. On Warm White use it for rules and fills, not text.
palettes.example: A private bank pitch: Warm White content slides, Charcoal section breaks with Champagne numerals.

palettes.name: Noir and Bronze Gold
palettes.contrast_notes: Flat gold is not foil; for metallic effect use a gradient from Bronze Gold to Ivory, and keep text solid.
palettes.example: A fragrance launch film end card: Noir ground, Bronze Gold monogram with a slow light sweep, Ivory tagline.

palettes.name: Emerald and Brass
palettes.contrast_notes: Brass reads at display size on Alabaster only. On Emerald, Brass is for frames and ornaments.
palettes.example: A heritage hotel brochure: Emerald cover with an Alabaster serif title, Brass keyline border, Alabaster inner pages.

palettes.name: Navy Trust
palettes.contrast_notes: Amber is a status or highlight color: as text only on Navy, on Cloud only as a fill with Ink text.
palettes.example: An investor update: Cloud slides, Navy headlines, Teal for actuals, Steel Grey for prior year, Amber to flag one risk.

palettes.name: Dark Technical
palettes.contrast_notes: Grid Line is structural only. Keep Cyan for the active or primary data series, Amber for one warning.
palettes.example: A chip architecture explainer: Void stage, Panel cards, Cyan data paths, one Amber bottleneck marker.

palettes.name: Blueprint
palettes.contrast_notes: Red Mark passes only at large size. Use it for callout circles and dimension highlights.
palettes.example: A product anatomy slide: Blueprint Blue ground, Line White outlines and labels, Cyan Line for hidden edges, Red Mark circling the key part.

palettes.name: Indigo Monochrome
palettes.contrast_notes: A single-hue ramp: keep text at least three steps from its ground. Add one neutral if a status color is needed.
palettes.example: A sequential chart: Indigo 200 to Indigo 900 for low to high values, Indigo 900 labels on Indigo 50.

palettes.name: Riso Overprint
palettes.contrast_notes: Inspired by risograph two-color printing; these are not official ink values. Simulate overprint with mix-blend-mode: multiply. Fluoro Pink is never text.
palettes.example: A gig flyer: Newsprint ground, Fluoro Pink and Overprint Blue shapes overlapping with multiply, Overlap Violet type.

palettes.name: Tomato and Mint Clash
palettes.contrast_notes: Near-complementary hues with similar lightness clash on purpose. Every text sits in Black or on a Black band.
palettes.example: A sneaker drop: Tomato full-bleed, Mint product silhouette, Black oversized type, Violet price sticker with Mint text.

palettes.name: Inkwell Sepia
palettes.contrast_notes: Faded Tone is for shading and panels only, never text on Aged Paper. Cartoon Red is a spot color (a bow, a nose, a title word), not a text color on Ink.
palettes.example: A coffee brand mascot sheet: Aged Paper ground, Ink line art with pie-cut eyes, Faded Tone shadows, Cartoon Red only on the mug.

palettes.name: Chrome Noir
palettes.contrast_notes: Flat Chrome is not metal: build the chrome look from a hard-stop gradient Void, Steel, Chrome, Ice Glint, keep text solid. Signal Red is one detail per image (an eye, a visor line).
palettes.example: A single cover: Void ground, a chrome figure lit from the top left with two star glints in Ice Glint, one Signal Red eye, title in condensed Chrome type.

palettes.name: Mid-century Warm
palettes.contrast_notes: Walnut on Cream is 11.4:1 and Teal on Cream 4.9:1, both fine for body text. Tangerine on Cream is 4.1:1, so use it for large type and shapes only. Mustard is a fill color: on Cream it is 1.9:1; set Walnut text on it (6.1:1).
palettes.example: A furniture catalogue cover: Cream ground, Tangerine boomerang and Teal starburst, Walnut headline, a Mustard price tag with Walnut text.

palettes.name: Neon Noir
palettes.contrast_notes: Neon White on Night is 17:1 and Electric Cyan on Night 11.9:1. Hot Pink on Night is 6.4:1 and Ultraviolet on Night 4.6:1, enough for text but keep glows off body copy. Neon White on Hot Pink is only 2.7:1: put Night text on Hot Pink buttons instead.
palettes.example: A night event poster: Night ground with a Hot Pink perspective grid, Electric Cyan title glow, Neon White details on a Dusk panel.

palettes.name: Aurora Haze
palettes.contrast_notes: Night Ink on Haze is 15.6:1 and Iris on Haze 5.6:1. Aqua Glow and Blossom are gradient and fill colors only: on Haze they reach 1.6:1 and 1.9:1. Put Night Ink text on them (10:1 and 8.3:1). On Iris use white text, not Night Ink (2.8:1).
palettes.example: An AI product hero: an aurora of Iris, Aqua Glow, and Blossom blurred over Haze, a frosted Lavender Mist card, Night Ink headline.

palettes.name: Electric Editorial
palettes.contrast_notes: Ink on Warm White is 17.5:1 and Electric Blue on Warm White 6.2:1, so blue can carry links and headlines. Vivid Orange (2.9:1) and Cyan (2.2:1) never carry text on Warm White: use them as fills with Ink text on top (6.1:1 and 8.0:1). On Electric Blue use Warm White text, not Ink (2.8:1).
palettes.example: A design-week site: Warm White pages, Ink headlines, Electric Blue links and section numbers, one Vivid Orange block per page with Ink text on it.

palettes.name: Jewel Tones
palettes.contrast_notes: Every jewel reads as text on Pearl (5.7:1 to 8.4:1), and Pearl reads on every jewel. Never set one jewel on another: they sit within 1.5:1 of each other. Use them as separate series or blocks divided by Pearl, and keep Onyx off the jewels (1.9:1 to 2.8:1).
palettes.example: An awards-night deck: Pearl slides, one jewel per award category, Onyx text, Pearl rules between jewel blocks.

palettes.name: Warm Minimalism
palettes.contrast_notes: Espresso on Oat is 13.3:1. Mushroom is a line and shape color only (2.3:1 on Oat). Walnut carries buttons and links (7.6:1 on Oat). There is no saturated accent on purpose: emphasis comes from Walnut fills and type weight.
palettes.example: A furniture lookbook: Oat pages, Beige image mats, Espresso text, Walnut buttons, Mushroom hairlines.

palettes.name: High Contrast (AAA)
palettes.contrast_notes: Every text pair reaches 7:1 (WCAG AAA) on White and Mist Grey: Near Black 19.7:1, Slate 9.8:1, Deep Blue 9.1:1, Burnt Orange 8.4:1. Focus Yellow is for focus rings and highlight backgrounds behind Near Black text (13.7:1), never for text (1.4:1 on White). Steel Line reaches 4.8:1 for borders and input outlines (WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1).
palettes.example: A benefits application form: White page, Mist Grey field groups, Near Black labels, Steel Line input borders, Deep Blue buttons, Focus Yellow focus ring.

palettes.name: Oxblood and Warm Cream
palettes.contrast_notes: Dark Brown on Warm Cream is 13.9:1 and Oxblood on Warm Cream is 10.9:1, so Oxblood can carry headlines, links, and buttons. Clay Taupe reaches only 4.2:1 on Warm Cream: use it for hairlines, icons, and large type, never body text. No metallic on purpose: the deep red is the only richness.
palettes.example: A leather goods lookbook: Warm Cream pages, Biscuit image mats, Dark Brown text, one Oxblood title per spread and Oxblood buttons on the web.

palettes.name: Midnight Navy and Pearl
palettes.contrast_notes: Pearl on Midnight Navy is 15.0:1. Cool Gray keeps 6.6:1 even on Night Slate, so captions stay readable on cards. Dusk Line is 1.9:1: rules and card edges only. Pale Steel Blue is the one accent; it replaces gold for cool evening luxury.
palettes.example: A watch launch page: Midnight Navy ground, the product lit in Pearl highlights, Cool Gray specifications, one Pale Steel Blue link.

palettes.name: Charcoal and Brushed Silver
palettes.contrast_notes: Warm White on Charcoal is 14.7:1. Brushed Silver is a flat light grey (8.7:1), not a metallic effect: use it for one rule, an icon, or a product highlight. Seam (1.9:1) is for card edges only.
palettes.example: A residential tower deck: Charcoal slides, Graphite plan panels, Warm White titles, Warm Grey notes, one Brushed Silver hairline under each title.

palettes.name: Dusty Rose and Cocoa
palettes.contrast_notes: Cocoa on Porcelain Rose is 11.5:1 and still 7.4:1 on Dusty Rose. Rosewood (5.3:1) carries buttons and links. Soft Taupe (2.1:1) is for hairlines only. Rose is a ground here, not an accent, which keeps it adult rather than sweet.
palettes.example: A skincare range: Porcelain Rose cartons, Dusty Rose inner trays, Cocoa type, Rosewood for the product name only.
